evidence_type: Read-only ADB pull and static REA/JADX analysis of the owner's updated, installed app; the app was not modified or re-signed
question: Does the actual Play-updated 2.6.1 build match the previously analyzed route, and does its signer match the retained 2.6.1 artifact?

acquisition.origin: Read-only ADB pull of the owner's existing installation after the owner updated from 2.4.1 to 2.6.1

files.name: base.apk
files.role: DEX code and manifest; analyzed here

files.name: split_config.arm64_v8a.apk
files.role: native library split; not needed for Java/Binder route

files.name: split_config.xxhdpi.apk
files.role: resource split; not needed for Java/Binder route

acquisition.note: Because the installed build is split, its base.apk hash is not directly comparable with the single-file APKPure 2.6.1 artifact. Signer identity is the useful comparison.

signature.signer_dn: CN=Android, OU=Android, O=Google Inc., L=Mountain View, ST=California, C=US
signature.comparison: Matches the certificate of the retained APKPure-labelled 2.6.1 APK. The earlier 2.4.1 installation used a different CN=Android Debug certificate; that discrepancy does not affect the updated Play build.

static_route_confirmation.authority: shipped-artifact / decompiled bytecode of the installed 2.6.1 base.apk

findings.fact: invokeSetCodec still resolves and invokes BluetoothA2dp.setCodecConfigPreference via reflection
LDAC quality constants are unchanged: 1000 optimized audio, 1001 balanced, 1002 optimized connection, 1003 best effort

CodecConfigFactory.build passes createLegacy(codecType, 1000000, sampleRate, bitsPerSample, channelMode, codecSpecific1, 0, 0, 0), confirming the platform constructor order discovered during the bounded shell attempt

limitations: Static code does not by itself establish runtime success; the owner's app-driven round-trip in codec-quality-roundtrip.json supplies that evidence.
No Frida trace was available on the non-debuggable Play build.
The reason the earlier 2.4.1 UI did not apply the change was not established.

privacy: APKs and full captures remain in the approved private temporary directory; only identities and selected decompiled facts are recorded here.
